title: BEVDet4D: Exploit Temporal Cues in Multi-camera 3D Object Detection
text: Warps the previous BEV feature by the ego transform (bilinear, rotation plus translation), concatenates it with the current one, adds a two-unit BEV encoder, and turns velocity into the positional offset between the two aligned features. nuScenes val Tiny: 39.2 to 44.0 NDS, mAVE 0.909 to 0.479 (0.328 with rotation, time-gap augmentation); an unaligned concatenation is worse than no history (37.6 NDS). Temporal part costs +1 M parameters, +7 GFLOPs, 15.6 to 15.5 FPS; aligning after the view transform is 2x faster than inside. For us the cheapest two-frame static memory; moving objects are only implicit in the feature difference.

title: Time Will Tell (SOLOFusion): long-term low-res BEV history plus short-term stereo
text: Stacks ego-aligned BEV maps of 16 past frames at 1/16 resolution into a cost volume and adds high-resolution plane-sweep stereo against the previous frame. nuScenes val: 0 / 1 / 16 / 41 past frames give NDS 0.347 / 0.423 / 0.474 / 0.467, so it saturates at 16; both streams 11.4 FPS, 3.6 GB against 17.6 FPS, 3.3 GB baseline. Parallel stacking grows with the window and has only ego warp for moving objects. For us: coarse long memory plus fine current frame; the stereo part needs a trainable image backbone.

title: VideoBEV: Exploring Recurrent Long-term Temporal Fusion for Multi-view 3D Perception
text: One recurrent BEV memory: H_i = [warp(H_i-1, ego); B_i] * V with a conv V that down-weights older frames, plus a time-gap embedding fused the same way for the velocity head. nuScenes val: history 0 / 1 / 4 / 16 / all gives NDS 0.382 / 0.450 / 0.471 / 0.489 / 0.492, mAVE 0.936 to 0.331; at 50 percent missed frames the time embedding removes 25 percent of the velocity error rise. Constant memory (one BEV map), overhead near the no-history model per a figure (no numbers in text). No moving-object gate. Template for our static hold with a learned decay.

title: BEVFormer: spatiotemporal transformers for BEV from multi-camera images
text: Temporal self-attention: previous BEV shifted by ego motion, deformable attention over queries and aligned history with offsets predicted from their concatenation, recurrent at test time. nuScenes val: 0.517 NDS / 0.416 mAP against 0.448 / 0.375 spatial-only, mAVE 0.802 to 0.394; ego alignment itself only +0.007 NDS. Latency 130 ms (6 layers), 25 ms (1 layer), 7 ms (single scale, 100 x 100 BEV, 1 layer), no temporal-only figure. The deformable offsets absorb object motion without a flow head; the cheaper descendants are VideoBEV and MemFusionMap.

title: RLG-TPV: Radar- and LiDAR-Guided Tri-Perspective View Fusion for Camera-Radar 3D Detection
text: Doppler-guided temporal fusion aligns past fused features with a motion field phi = s * Smooth(v_radar) + learned residual, gated by sigmoid((speed - tau_v)/T) so cells without measured motion get no extra warp; occupancy gate on weak features; four keyframes at 1 s. nuScenes val 0.4981 mAP / 0.5959 NDS; the DGTF block adds +0.0013 mAP / +0.0040 NDS, which the authors call within noise; one keyframe instead of four costs -11.5 percent mAP. No cost figures, no code, ego compensation of Doppler unspecified. Gate form is the transferable part.

title: 4DR360: State Reasoning for Joint 3D Detection and Occupancy Prediction in 4D Radar-Camera Perception
text: Doppler-guided temporal fusion caches state, occupancy, pose and a BEV motion field of the last frames; ego alignment, then a dynamic warp by clipped velocity from the decoded velocity map corrected with radar Doppler, confidence-weighted decay average, residual Conv3D update. ManTruckScenes 4 frames: no temporal 47.45 mAP / 50.89 NDS, ego align only 47.12 / 50.45 (below no history), state memory 49.06 / 52.28, plus Doppler warp 49.57 / 52.97, mAVE 1.0213 to 0.9442. Whole model 4.5 - 5.5 FPS, no DTF-specific cost. Shows ego warp alone does not help and the Doppler warp is a second-order gain.

title: AttentiveGRU: Recurrent Spatio-Temporal Modeling for Radar-Based BEV Object Detection
text: Radar BEV memory buffer fused with the present frame by 32 latent queries per block (3 blocks, width 64), median-thresholded cross-attention gates, 1x1 conv gates on overlaps and a deformable conv for non-overlap regions; no ego pose input. nuScenes car class: 32.4 to 39.2 mAP (+21 percent relative) with CenterPoint Transformer, gains largest for moving classes, weaker for large stationary vehicles. T=2 on nuScenes, one 2080Ti, no cost or ablation numbers. Co-authored by the user (Meuter). Ego-free alignment is weaker than an exact warp when the pose is known.

title: Redefining Radar Segmentation: Static-Moving Segmentation and Ego-Motion Estimation from Radar Point Clouds
text: Per-point MLP + GRU over 8 raw radar scans gives static and moving probabilities; static returns follow a sine relation of radial velocity and azimuth, a weighted least-squares fit gives sensor velocity and re-weights the static set. RadarScenes: moving IoU 0.86, F1 0.92; ego RMSE 0.37 cm/s (vx), 0.12 deg/s (yaw rate); 0.15 M parameters. With our known ego velocity the expected static Doppler is a closed formula, so a moving mask needs no network. Not shown on nuScenes radar; no code.

title: MotionNet: Joint Perception and Motion Prediction from BEV Maps
text: Five ego-aligned LiDAR sweeps as 13 x 256 x 256 occupancy, a pyramid network with pseudo-1D temporal convs, per-cell class, 1 s motion and static probability; motion zeroed on background and on static foreground. nuScenes LiDAR: motion error static 0.026 m, slow 0.257 m, fast 1.074 m; ego sync matters (0.257 to 0.425 without); 19 ms per inference. Background temporal-consistency loss across ego-aligned frames is a label-free signal for the static part. LiDAR input, bicycles weak.

title: FIERY: Future Instance Prediction in Bird's-Eye View from Surround Monocular Cameras
text: Camera BEV on 200 x 200 at 0.5 m, past states warped by a spatial transformer with ego-motion as extra channels, 3D-conv temporal model (64 x 200 x 200 state), ConvGRU for the future, heads for centerness, offset, segmentation and flow, instances linked by flow-warped centers. nuScenes 2 s: IoU 59.4 / 36.7, VPQ 50.2 / 29.9 against a static model 47.9 / 30.3 and 43.1 / 24.5; about 8.1 M parameters, no inference latency. The recipe at our grid size; instance flow is the moving-object handle; future prediction out of scope.

title: MemFusionMap: Working Memory Fusion for Online Vectorized HD Map Construction
text: Fixed-lag buffer of 4 ego-warped BEV frames plus a warped overlap heatmap (cell age, start all ones, +1 per step) turned into 32 channels, fused with a dilated conv block and LayerNorm. nuScenes mAP against StreamMapNet 34.1 to 38.0 (60 x 30 m) and 22.2 to 27.6 (100 x 50 m); 15.1 against 15.3 FPS. Static map content only, no moving-object path. The age channel and bounded memory are cheap and transfer to a lane BEV memory.
